today.description: Keep your agents and builds running on a Mac mini or Studio. Beam brings their Terminal, browser and other app windows onto the Mac in front of you, each as its own window with a Dock icon and ⌘Tab presence. Encrypted between your Macs. Free to try.

today.name: Beam
today.tagline: Highly efficient agentic 501B parameter open model
today.description: Beam is a sparse Mixture-of-Experts model with 501 billion total parameters, 23 billion active, built for coding, reasoning, and agentic workloads.

comments.text: Beam is focused on coding and agentic use cases. It is for teams that want a frontier-scale model on their own hardware, infrastructure, or cloud, and want to customize it to their own use cases. Beam ships with its own dedicated open source Rust based harness that delivers the best performance from the model.TL;DR501B-parameter MoEs LLM with 23B active per token. 52 layers, 256 experts per MoE layer, 8 routed per token.Text in, text out with context window of 1M tokens.Checkpoint formats: BF16, FP8, and NVFP4Reasoning that can stay in context across turns (`preserve_thinking`), tool calling with a dedicated grammar. The model supports five reasoning values: "low", "medium" (default), "high", "xhigh", and "max".Response template in the tokenizer.Speculative decoding drafter model with DFlash2Day-0 libraries: transformers, SGLang, vLLM. Full-parameter RL with Miles.Ships with an open source Rust-based custom harness.Apache 2.0.

yesterday.description: An open-source hook and local proxy for Claude Code, Codex, Copilot CLI and VS Code. In Claude Code it masks secrets and personal data in tool results before the model reads them, and shim watch shows what a session sent and cost. No account, no telemetry.

comments.text: Hi Product Hunt, I'm Mertcan, one of the makers of shim-cli.We built it because we wanted to see what our own coding agents send to the model. A request carries a lot more than your prompt: the system prompt and the tools array, plus every file the agent read along the way. When the agent opens a .env, the keys in it go to the model too, and nothing in the session tells you.shim-cli sits next to the agent you already use and runs on your machine:• shim install claude adds hooks to Claude Code. When a tool result holds an API key, a password, an email, an IBAN, a phone number or a Turkish ID number, the model gets a placeholder like <SECRET_1> instead.• shim watch -- claude runs one session through a local proxy and prints where the input tokens went, what the session cost (or would cost on an API key), and which sensitive values were in the request and the response. It forwards every byte unchanged.There's no account and no telemetry, and the hook adds no network destination. Codex, GitHub Copilot CLI and VS Code are supported too, with less coverage.What it cannot do, so you know before you install:• A prompt you type into Claude Code or Codex is not masked, because neither client lets a hook rewrite it. shim reports it, or stops it under enforce. Copilot CLI does get the masked prompt.• In Claude Code, shell commands, the output of a failed command and files attached with @ are reported, not masked.• Codex and Copilot CLI tool traffic is not inspected, and VS Code only reports.• Detection is best effort and misses some values. It is not a DLP boundary.• macOS and Linux only. Windows is first on our list.Try it in a minute:uv tool install --python 3.12 shimshim demo claudeshim install claudeIt's Apache-2.0 on GitHub. The feedback we want most: what shim missed in your own sessions, and which client we should go deeper on next.

comments.text: We're launching 3AM today: an AI on-call engineer for the systems you can't rewrite. Three things shaped it:Engineers needed proof, not a guess. Banks, insurers and telcos can't send production data to someone else's cloud, and their regulators ask where every byte goes. So 3AM runs inside your network with no inbound ports, works fully air-gapped too, and the only thing that ever reaches us is a signed licence check. Literally.Everyone needed to stay in charge. Nobody wants an AI changing production on its own in the middle of the night. So every fix is rehearsed with a dry run first, then waits for a person's approval in Slack, Symphony, PagerDuty, xMatters or email (you name it). 3AM starts in shadow mode: it watches, proposes fixes and changes nothing. Giving it more autonomy takes two approvers. And every step goes on a hash-chained audit log your auditors can verify.Proof is the point. We test 3AM by breaking a real open-source core banking system, 244,000 lines of ten-year-old Java, on purpose, in 67 different ways. Every number we publish comes from those runs, and zero harmful actions is a release gate, not a target.If you or your team is fed up of prod being down at night (or even during the day), 3AM is for you!🎁 As a bonus, the first 90 days are on us! Try it, tell us where it falls short, and we'll fix it.Note that 3AM is AI, and in its open alpha stage. Full disclosure — I'm a big fan of Anthropic and actually built an app that works exclusively with Claude Desktop for secure local file search. So I've spent a lot of time thinking about this space.My concern with Cowork isn't the vision, it's the architecture. Agentic tasks burn through tokens fast (Anthropic says so themselves), so that $200/month cap can disappear quicker than you'd expect. And at that price, you'd want to use it for real work — but the whole thing requires giving Claude direct read/write/delete access to your files. If you're handling client data, patient records, or anything regulated, you're basically out.The bigger issue is prompt injection. Anthropic admits "the chances of an attack are still non-zero" — and back in October 2025, researchers showed exactly that: a prompt injection against Claude that pulled up to 30MB of user data per request through Anthropic's own API. When you're talking about an agent with file system access, email connectors, and a browser, that's not some theoretical edge case.There's a reason some of us build tools where Claude can search your files without actually touching them. The agentic future is definitely coming, but "AI that can access everything" and "AI that keeps you in control" are two very different products for two very different users.
